children: Schwab’s latest sector outlook points to a broader spending-driven boost for Industrials and Materials over the next six to 12 months, while weaker consumer fundamentals and continued pressure on commercial real estate weigh on its outlook for Consumer Discretionary and Real Estate.

According to the latest Schwab research, Industrials should benefit from increased capital spending on electricity capacity, construction tied to AI infrastructure, defense, and energy. Higher costs and potential delays in data center construction could, however, temper growth.

Materials are also supported by these trends, with tight supplies of copper and other metals providing a favorable backdrop. Schwab flagged uneven demand and weakness in areas such as lithium as risks.

Healthcare is expected to benefit from technological advances and improving operational efficiency, particularly in biotechnology. Schwab cautioned that results can vary considerably depending on clinical trials and regulatory decisions.

Financials are seeing upward earnings revisions, supported by a steeper yield curve, solid net interest income, and improved capital markets activity. Uncertainty around central bank policy decisions remains a risk to the sector.
Energy earnings have risen sharply on higher oil prices, leading to earnings upgrades. Schwab noted that some of those gains could reverse if geopolitical tensions ease.

Communication Services remains less favored despite continued strength in digital advertising and opportunities tied to AI. Elevated valuations, heavy investment spending, and uncertainty around returns on investment could create challenges for the sector.

Consumer Staples is rated neutral, with attractive valuations, relatively steady demand, and limited exposure to the increasingly crowded AI trade providing support. Further price increases could encourage more cost-sensitive consumers to trade down, Schwab said.
Information Technology is rated neutral by Schwab.

Utilities are rated less favored. Rising electricity demand could support the sector, but higher financing costs, regulatory uncertainty, and public pushback related to data centers could weigh on performance.

Consumer Discretionary is rated least favored, as softer revenue and free cash flow have weakened its fundamentals relative to other cyclical sectors. Low consumer confidence is also expected to continue weighing on the group.

Real Estate is also least favored as the commercial office segment continues to face supply imbalances that have persisted since the COVID-19 pandemic. After a strong start to the year, the sector has weakened amid rate increases.

title: Schwab sees stronger prospects for industrials, and materials as consumer confidence falters
